title: A header value with no single spelling every language agrees on is refused at the call.
why: behavioural spec 'request' (ADR 0019): every value other than a string, an integral number or a boolean is refused at the call, before any document is built — because a value whose spelling differs by language ('1' or '1.0'; '1e+21' or '1.0E21') would make two SDKs send different bytes for the same test, and a date has no format the SDK may choose.
note: A fractional number stands for the whole refused class here, because it is the one every language can write and none spell alike. The case is that no document is produced; how a language refuses — a thrown error, a failed build — is the style guide's business.

interaction.description: a header value the SDK cannot spell
